header.deal: Retailer with stores and a website (120 stores)
header.tag_why: The COO who signed was weighing one system for the tills and the website, a store rollout and a till return she could watch, and we described those where Adyen reportedly brought a retail rollout team, one contract and retailers she knew.

messaging_changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
messaging_changes.change: For retailers with stores and a website, say: 'One system for the tills and the website: one customer, one basket.' Say 'tills', not 'point of sale' or 'in-person payments'. Back the line with a live, step-by-step demo of an online order being returned at a store till, not a diagram, and only use it once that demo is confirmed to run live.
messaging_changes.why: Our unified commerce slide met silence and was dismissed as 'that's a diagram', the customer described the need as 'One system for the tills and the website' and 'one customer, one basket', and they asked to watch a till return live, which we only described.

messaging_changes.change: For COO and store-operations buyers on store rollouts, add a rollout proof point: a standard rollout plan with dates, who installs, and what happens to the old tills, plus the named people accountable for the rollout on our side. Never answer 'who does the installs' with an unnamed partner.
messaging_changes.why: The deal turned when the store-operations lead heard 'we'd bring in a partner' and stopped asking questions, the customer asked for a rollout plan covering 'Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills', and by Raj's secondhand account Adyen brought people who had done store rollouts.

messaging_changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
messaging_changes.change: For retail decision-makers, offer a reference call with a retailer running stores and online with us, and line it up early so it is ready when asked. Use customer stories to support the call, not to replace it.
messaging_changes.why: The decider's side asked 'can I talk to them?' and we 'couldn't set up a call in time', while Adyen reportedly named retailers Angela knew.

evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: they'd just launched a loyalty program that was supposed to work everywhere and didn't, because store and web were two different customer records.
evidence.label: fact

trigger.insight: The trigger was a store-floor failure: returns, a broken loyalty program and split customer records. It was not a checkout or conversion problem. The origin story everyone there tells puts the COO in a store, which pointed to who owned the pain long before the signature did, even though the RFP sat with the CTO.
trigger.messaging: Open retail deals with buy online, return in store and one customer record for loyalty, not with checkout conversion or the global-currency opener (M1).

decider.messaging: Build a COO and store-operations message track about accountability, rollout and the till experience, and run it in parallel with the CTO and RFP track instead of assuming the RFP owner is the buyer.

By his account, Adyen answered the question the stores side was really asking: who will do this, on how many contracts, and who else has done it. After that meeting the evaluation flipped from web to stores, and we kept competing on the web side, which was not deciding the deal.
competitor.messaging: Lead with named store-rollout people, a single contract and referenceable retailers in our own words, before a competitor makes the evaluation about stores.

decided.insight: The deal turned in a workshop requested by the decider's team. We sent two people to face six store-operations staff, and 'we'd bring in a partner' was the answer that ended their questions. Being ahead meant being ahead on the web side according to Raj, which was the half of the deal not being decided.
decided.messaging: Never answer 'who does the installs' with an unnamed partner; name the installer, the rollout team and their store track record, and own accountability on one contract.

gaps.insight: The customer made three proof requests: a reference call, a rollout plan and a live return. We met each one with a document or a description. M8's 'see our customer stories' is exactly what failed, because the decider wanted to talk to the customer, not read about them. The transcript does not establish whether we could have shown the till return live or simply did not.
gaps.messaging: Rewrite M8 to promise a reference call with a retailer running stores and online on us, and back M3 with a standard rollout plan and a demo-ready till return.

language.insight: The customer's words are physical and about accountability: tills, one basket, no finger-pointing. Ours are category labels they never used. Angela's 'two vendors pointing at each other' is the risk our partner-install answer created, whether or not she said it in response to that answer.
language.messaging: Rewrite M3 in their words, for example 'One system for the tills and the website: one customer, one basket, one team accountable', and say 'tills' instead of 'point of sale'.

gaps.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom, and Raj if he will take a loss call: what did Angela weigh in the final decision, and did Raj actually recommend us to her?

gaps.question: What did you say when Bev asked how a return works at the till?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom and the solutions engineer exactly what was described, and whether we can demo a buy-online, return-at-till flow live today.

gaps.question: Which retailers did Adyen name, and what did the one contract cover?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Raj which retailers Adyen referenced and what they offered for rollout and till support.

gaps.question: Did Adyen take both web and stores, or is the online business still open?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom what exactly Angela signed with Adyen and whether any online scope remains for us.

gaps.question: What were they using before for tills and web?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom who the incumbent providers were for stores and online.

gaps.question: Why couldn't we set up the reference call in time?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom and customer marketing what blocked the reference call and how long it would normally take.

close.rep_takeaway: The pain lived with the COO, whose stores had the returns queue, and she signed. You met her once and ran the deal through the RFP owner. When 11 of 14 questions turned to stores, that was the signal to bring store-rollout people, a live till return and a reference call, not a description and 'a partner'.
